label: Kant's thesis is the rival of the EXISTENCE_8 real-predicate premise
note: Target: the real-predicate premise of Meditation V. Mechanism: if existence is not a determination of a concept, the concept of the supremely perfect contains no existence feature and the step from the concept to existence fails; the real-predicate control (b) is a model of that situation. Independent justification offered for the thesis (navigation, attribution deferred): the concept of a hundred possible thalers and of a hundred actual thalers have the same content, so existence adds no determination; on the reconstruction, existence is positing (EXISTENCE_1). The thesis is a rival, not a checked refutation: neither statement is derived here. No substantive objection from this thesis is identified against the a posteriori root routes, whose existence premises are about what exists and do not take existence as part of a concept; Kant's separate scope objection to their causal premises is recorded in docs/kant-cosmological-inference.md.
